messages:
Marta: Noticed a recurring tail-latency blip on dedicated pool `dedicated-phi-7` in us-east-1 around 15:03 UTC. Looks networking-y, not GPU thermal.
Ryan: pool id? any host-level anomalies?
Marta: hosts: gpu-phi-7-{01..04}. NIC drops and txq growth on host-02. CPU irq spikes too.
Anika: Any recent tenant activity spikes?
Marta: Yes 15:01 a tenant kicked off multi-GB prefetches into local cache (s3) for a large eval run.
Ops-Bot: Alert: egress-saturation on gpu-phi-7-02 (15:03 UTC). Auto-evac queued 1 pod.
Samir: Sounds like noisy-transfer vs latency-sensitive inferencing on same host. We should throttle heavy downloads for non-latency tenants.
Ryan: Quick triage: can someone run `ethtool -S eth0` on host-02 and `ss -tnp` to find long-lived flows?
Anika: On it. Also starting iperf3 between host-02 and a staging client to reproduce.
Marta: ethtool shows tx_packets high, tx_errors 0 but tx_queue_len climbing. Kernel qdisc backlog grows.
Anika: I can push a transient qdisc limiter: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root tbf rate 5gbit burst 64k latency 30ms` and watch behavior.
Ling: For customers on Dedicated we promised "isolation" - should we consider egress-carve or per-pool egress policing? Product needs a note.
Samir: Carving egress per pool has capacity/cost implications. If we throttle at host-level we risk underutilizing uplinks. Need cost estimate.
Ryan: Short-term: apply tc on host-02 and move the heavy downloader to shared-burst. Medium-term: allocator should be NIC-aware: if host txq > threshold avoid packing new latency tenants.
Anika: Applied tc on host-02. Monitoring now.
Marta: After tc, tail latency on that pool dropped ~35% in 3m, allocator evictions stopped.
Ops-Bot: Job complete: tc-apply host-02 by Anika (job-id jc-772).
Anika: eBPF snapshot shows long-lived TCP flows from tenant A; I annotated flow_id in artifacts.
Marta: Action items: 1) add host txq metric to placement preflight, 2) add tenant prefetch throttling flag in manager, 3) RFC for per-dedicated-pool egress policy.
Ling: I'll spin up RFC draft with SLA implications.
Samir: I'll produce a back-of-envelope cost model: reserved egress vs reactive reroute overhead.
Ryan: Ops note: consider irqbalance and XPS tuning to reduce IRQ steal under heavy tx. Also test token bucket sizes across rack uplinks.
Anika: Also propose a small daemon that watches for >120s flows >1Gbps and labels tenant as "bulk-transfer" to inform allocator.
Marta: Okay writing incident note and attaching tc command, iperf logs, ethtool output. Nice rollback path: remove tc if we see regressions.
Ryan: Nice quick mitigation. Keep an eye for recurrence.
Marta: End."
